I'm 61 years old this year, and I've been farming these flat fields in Quzhou County since I was a teenager. I finished middle school, so I can read the instructions on seed bags and fertilizer packs well enough, but my real knowledge comes from forty years of working this land on the North China Plain. My family has about 6 mu of good irrigated land, and at my age I don't gamble with new crops or fancy experiments—I stick with what I know will put food on the table and leave a little cash in my pocket.

My wheat is already in the ground. I sowed Luyuan502 last October, which is an improved variety that handles our cold winters well and gives me steady yields. I prepared the land with the rotary tiller before sowing to get a fine seedbed. This wheat will come off in early June, and the day after harvest I will plant Denghai605 maize hybrid directly into the stubble without plowing. No-tillage saves me diesel, time, and my back. Denghai605 is what all my neighbors grow too—it is a reliable hybrid that yields well if I give it water at the right times.

For fertilizer, I follow what the county extension agent recommends, but I don't overdo it because prices are too high. For my wheat, I apply about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu total, split between basal compound fertilizer at sowing and urea topdressing at green-up in spring, plus around 11 kg of phosphate and 4 kg of potash per mu. For the summer maize, I use compound fertilizer at sowing—about 12 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphate, and 3 kg potash per mu. That is enough for this soil.

Water is precious and electricity for the pump costs money. I irrigate the wheat four times: the winter irrigation to protect against freezing, then again at jointing, heading, and grain-filling. The maize only needs two good irrigations, at the big-flare stage and during grain filling. For chemicals, I spray my wheat four times total—herbicide once after sowing, insecticide twice for aphids and armyworms, and fungicide once at heading to prevent rust. For maize, I spray herbicide once, insecticide twice for corn borers, and use a plant growth regulator once to keep the stalks from lodging in the summer storms. I expect about 1000 kg per mu from the wheat and 1100 kg per mu from the maize if the weather is normal.
